title: Patrick Mahomes throws 5 TD passes as Chiefs roll past Falcons
content:
ATLANTA — No Kenneth Walker III, no problem for the Kansas City Chiefs. Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes, including one to newly acquired wide receiver Josh Downs, and the Chiefs dominated the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 on Sunday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Mahomes showed no ill effects from the sprained right elbow he suffered in Week 9, completing 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards and the five scores.

Walker, the NFL’s second-leading rusher, sat out Sunday’s game with a groin injury, but backup Emmett Johnson filled in capably. Johnson finished with 101 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards and two touchdown receptions.

Downs, acquired from the Indianapolis Colts in a trade-deadline day deal, caught four passes for 53 yards and a pretty 18-yard touchdown pass from Mahomes. Rookie Cyrus Allen had a 39-yard TD catch, and Andrew Armstrong added a 43-yarder.

The Falcons struggled to get anything going on offense until the game was out of hand. The Chiefs held running back Bijan Robinson to 71 yards on 16 carries and a fourth-quarter touchdown. The other bright spot for Atlanta was wide receiver Drake London, who had six catches for 109 yards, including a 38-yard grab.

The Falcons briefly gave the home crowd hope late in the fourth quarter with the first recovery of an onside kick in the NFL this season. They followed with a Jake Moody field goal to cut the deficit to two scores before the Chiefs finished them off.

Spectacular — especially given the circumstances and knowing Mahomes was playing through an elbow sprain he suffered last week.

The Chiefs entered the game with several offensive injuries; they were starting two backup offensive tackles and were also down Walker, who was ruled out with a groin injury after entering the week as the NFL’s second-leading rusher.

Early Sunday, the Chiefs offense lost more depth. Right guard Trey Smith left in the first half with a concussion, and tight end Travis Kelce missed most of the first half after rolling his ankle.

None of it seemed to slow down Mahomes, who was decisive and accurate throughout. His preliminary Pro Football Focus passing grade was one of his top marks of the season, and he avoided negative plays, throwing the ball away when his protection broke down.

Mahomes also delivered a few of his best deep passes of the season. He hit Downs on a pinpoint back-shoulder throw late in the second quarter, then backed that up with deep strikes to Allen, Armstrong and Rashee Rice. — Jesse Newell, Chiefs beat writer

That’s a really hard list to rank because it was bad across the board and right from the start.

The Falcons started the game with four consecutive three-and-outs and have 26 of those since Week 5, more than any other team in the league in that span. The offensive line was flagged for seven penalties, and at one point, CBS analyst J.J. Watt was calling out whether Atlanta was running or passing before the snap based on right tackle Jawaan Taylor’s sets.

The Falcons have committed a league-high 14 offensive penalties in the last two weeks. They finished 5-for-16 on third down and only one of their first 10 possessions made it to Chiefs territory. Robinson had just one touch on the first two offensive possessions and finished with 16 rushes for 71 yards and four catches for 6 yards.

Subtracting the Falcons’ surprising offensive explosion in two primetime games in Weeks 3 and 4, Atlanta is 31st in the league in scoring (14.3 ppg).

“I don’t think you have to worry about the fight of this football team,” Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said. “Our guys understand what is in front of us. All of this falls on me. I will take responsibility for everything that happens on this football team.”

Offensive coordinator and play caller Tommy Rees moved from the coaching box to the sideline Sunday for the first time this season, but it did not help. The way things are going, Falcons fans may lobby for him to be completely out of the stadium when this team returns to the field after a bye next week. That game will be against the Vikings defense, by the way. — Josh Kendall, Falcons beat writer

The fact that the Chiefs played so well, even without one of their top offensive threats.

Walker — deservingly — has been in the Offensive Player of the Year race, showing excellent tackle-breaking ability as the Chiefs have revolutionized their run game this season.

Without him, though, Johnson, the fifth-round rookie, played about as well as K.C. could’ve hoped.

In his first NFL start, Johnson scored twice and surpassed 150 scrimmage yards. He also showed his typical shiftiness, leading the team with four combined missed tackles, per PFF’s preliminary data.

Downs also had an immediate impact after this week’s trade, earning Mahomes’ trust when he caught a contested pass in the end zone for his second-quarter touchdown.

The Chiefs averaged more than 7 yards per play before garbage time, displaying flashes of dominance even while playing short-handed. — Newell

Not a lot in the first half and then a tremendous amount down the stretch. Safety DeMarcco Hellams, who took Bates’ place in the starting lineup after Atlanta traded its best defensive player to Jacksonville last week, led the Falcons with 11 tackles, and the defense kept the game close for three quarters.

The Chiefs led just 14-3 at the break and got their second touchdown only because Atlanta was flagged for offsides on a field goal attempt. The Falcons then forced punts on each of Kansas City’s first two drives of the second half before things got out of hand. The Chiefs’ next three possessions resulted in touchdowns and chewed up 212 yards. — Kendall

It’s getting better … and is trending toward becoming a top-10 unit.

The pass rush has improved most over the last two weeks. After a five-sack effort against the Jets, K.C. added three more Sunday, constantly collapsing the pocket around Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. while forcing him into uncomfortable situations. Defensive end George Karlaftis, meanwhile, continued his ascent in a career year with 1.5 sacks and a pass knockdown.

Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo also deserves credit for having his defense ready for Robinson, as the NFL’s leading rusher found few creases or cutback lanes. — Newell
